subject: RE: Tiger Labs — Dedicated GPU Commitment & Margin Concession
messages:
From: Ava Rodriguez <ava@tigerlabs.ai>
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: salesops@tigerlabs.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated proposal follow-up and question on credits

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Tiger Labs is excited about Redwood’s latency profile. We ran the numbers internally and have two asks before we can move ahead:

1) We plan to commit to a 6‑month reserved pool sized for ~150 peak concurrent sessions (avg seq len ~512). Can you confirm how that maps to the Dedicated SKU sizing matrix and whether you offer a throughput SLA for sustained bursts?

2) Competitor X provided a one‑time onboarding credit that offsets our first month of consumption. Given the strategic fit (we plan to route 3 product lines to your endpoint), is Redwood open to a comparable one‑time credit or adjusted T&Cs on the first invoice?

Attached is a CSV with our observed traffic patterns. We are under a tight procurement timeline and need to confirm financials by July 5.

Best,
Ava Rodriguez\Head of Platform Partnerships\Tiger Labs
attachments: traffic-patterns-q1-q2.csv (text/csv)

From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: Ava Rodriguez <ava@tigerlabs.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated proposal follow-up and question on credits

Ava — thanks for the data and the clear timeline. Quick answers:

- SKU sizing: based on 150 concurrent sessions at ~512 tokens, I recommend a 10‑GPU A100 equivalent pool with sustained burst headroom; that aligns to our "D-10" reserved SKU. I’ll attach the mapping for your procurement team.
- Throughput SLA: we provide a 95th percentile per‑token latency SLO and can agree a throughput commitment for sustained bursts (we commonly define burst windows and provision headroom in the contract).

On the credit ask: we do have flexibility for strategic accounts, but that requires a short approval loop for a one‑time onboarding credit. I’m looping in Laura (RevOps) and Priyom (Sales Lead) to scope the ask and confirm internal approvals.

Next steps: Laura — can you confirm what one‑time credit % we can entertain against a 12‑month equivalent commit? Priyom — happy to sync if you want to align on commercial levers (commit length, billing cadence, pilot thresholds).

Michael
Director, Strategic Accounts\Redwood Inference
attachments: dedicated-sku-mapping.pdf (application/pdf)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Ava Rodriguez <ava@tigerlabs.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated proposal follow-up and question on credits

Thanks, Michael. Quick internal note: a one‑time credit is handled as a contra‑revenue item and typically needs manager sign‑off for anything over $40k. If the customer is willing to convert the pilot into a 12‑month reserved commit (billed monthly) at the D‑10 level, we can consider a credit between 5–10% of first‑month ARR or a fixed onboarding credit.

Priyom, help me understand the upsell pathway — how confident is Tiger Labs at committing to 12 months vs 6? Also, what are the margin implications for Redwood if we include a month‑one credit plus an elevated SLA?

Laura Bennett\Senior RevOps Manager\Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: Ava Rodriguez <ava@tigerlabs.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated proposal follow-up and question on credits

Looping in Marissa from Sales Strategy to weigh on concession playbook. Internal read: Tiger Labs is strategic — multi‑product routing, strong growth signal. They indicated procurement prefers 6 months, but legal/procurement flexibility may shift if we make the commercial language favorable.

Proposed concession structure to present to customer:
- If Tiger signs a 6‑month commitment at D‑10 now with an explicit option to extend to 12 months within the first 90 days, Redwood will provide:
  * A one‑time onboarding credit equal to 7% of the committed monthly ARR (applied to month 1 invoice), OR
  * Alternatively, waive the first month’s minimum committed usage fee (equivalent $ value in invoice credit).
- If Tiger converts to 12 months within 90 days, we’ll apply an additional 3% renewal credit to month 1 of the 12‑month period.
- SLA: commit to a throughput policy with burst buckets; small escrow of extra capacity for first 60 days.

If you approve this construct, I’ll draft term language and request an executive sign‑off for the credit band. Marissa — please note margin impact and any higher‑level exceptions.

Priyom Das\Enterprise AE\Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: Ava Rodriguez <ava@tigerlabs.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated proposal follow-up and question on credits

Looks reasonable from a GTM perspective. Margin check: at D‑10 pricing our blended unit margin after hardware and network costs is tight. A one‑time 7% onboarding credit is acceptable if we secure the explicit 90‑day conversion clause and add a 10% price uplift if they request a hard SLA greater than our standard SLO for burst windows.

I suggest we route the 7% credit for executive approval (VP RevOps signoff) and add two protective clauses in the term sheet: 1) usage minimums for month 1 to avoid credit gaming; 2) termination fee if they exit before 90 days after conversion to 12 months.

Marissa Cole\Head of Sales Strategy\Redwood Inference

From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Ava Rodriguez <ava@tigerlabs.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Tiger Labs — Dedicated GPU Commitment & Margin Concession

Team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Laura: please open the exec approval ticket using the attached term sheet (I added the 7% onboarding credit line and the 90‑day conversion option; see comments on usage minimums). I’ve included the DocuSign link for faster signature routing.

Ava — per our internal review, Redwood can offer the 7% onboarding credit applied to month 1 if Tiger signs the 6‑month D‑10 reserved commit with the conversion option. We’ll include the protective clauses Marissa recommended (usage floor + termination fee). SLA/throughput language will be appended to the SOW.

Next: Laura will route this for VP sign‑off; we expect a response within 48 hours. If approved, we’ll send a final term sheet + DocuSign envelope. Appreciate the quick timeline from your side.

Michael Grant\Director, Strategic Accounts\Redwood Inference
attachments: tiger-dedicated-term-sheet-v2.pdf (application/pdf); docusign-approval-link: https://docusign.net/TL/exec-approval-456
